title: Maryam, the only woman named
hook: Maryam is the only woman named in the Qur'an, and a surah bears her name

segments.voice: Yesterday: wudu, and your line, water is mercy. Today a new thread through the book: its women.

Read the Qur'an looking only for women, and you'll find a lot of them. A queen who rules a kingdom. A mother who sets her baby on a river. A wife who argues her case and is heard. A wife who laughs at the news that she'll have a son. They speak, they choose, they pray. But almost none of them is named. They're the wife of, the mother of, the sister of, a woman. Except one. Her name appears more often in the Qur'an than in the whole New Testament, and a surah is called by it.

Maryam. Mary, the mother of 'Isa, Jesus. By the usual count her name appears thirty-four times, and surah nineteen bears it. Why her? The Qur'an doesn't explain its choice, and scholars have offered reasons rather than one answer. But look at how it speaks of her. In Al 'Imran the angels say: Allah has chosen you and purified you, and chosen you above the women of all the worlds. As a girl in the temple's prayer niche, she's found with provision no one brought her, and when Zakariyya asks where it came from, she answers simply: from Allah. Then the hardest scene. Surah nineteen says the pains of labor drove her, alone, to the trunk of a palm tree, and she cried that she wished she'd died before this and been forgotten. Forgotten, of all words. And she's answered: a stream is set beneath her, the palm will drop fresh dates if she shakes it, so eat, drink and be comforted. When she brings the child home and her people accuse her, she doesn't argue. She points to the baby, and the baby speaks. One more detail. Her son is called, again and again, 'Isa ibn Maryam, Jesus son of Mary. In a culture that named people by their fathers, he is named by his mother. Christians honor her too, with their own ways of speaking about her. In the Qur'an, the woman who feared being forgotten is the one whose name it keeps.

segments.voice: Let one woman come to mind whose care made you who you are, a mother, a grandmother, a teacher, a neighbor, even if few people know it. Say her name slowly, and recall one specific thing she did: a meal, a word, a night she sat up with you. If she has died and you pray, you can ask mercy for her; if she's alive, just hold her in mind with thanks.
Maryam. The only woman named in the Qur'an, chosen above the women of the worlds, and the mother whose name her son carries. Today's word.
Your line: named. Named about thirty-four times, and a surah of her own. Day six hundred seventy-one, done.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Maryam as one of the greatest women; Maryam is a common name for Muslim girls, and surah Maryam is widely recited and memorized.
